💡 Key Takeaways
  • England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne.
  • Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’.
  • Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne.

Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’.

Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.

Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted with the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, saying afterwards that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.

Industry observers note that A club statement on X remarked: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”.

The Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired the visitors ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled things up when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half, and Noted El Mala missed an excellent late chance to earn Cologne’s first win at Bayern since 2009.

It has been revealed that the 33-year-old may face a race to be fit for the Nations League quarter-finals, with the first leg in Norway taking place on 27 March – just over four months away. The Bayern sporting director, Max Eberl, said on Friday that club doctors were “presently discussing whether or not to recommend surgery” for Kane’s injury.

It has been revealed that part of Kane’s recovery period will come during the Bundesliga’s winter break from 20 December to 8 January. He will, however, miss Champions League games away to Lille next week and at home to Slavia Prague next month, as well as the January trip to Manchester United and the league phase finale at home to Real Betis.

Industry observers note that kane’s setback adds to an extensive Bayern injury list, with Michael Olise also going off during Friday’s game with a foot contusion. Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and Manuel Neuer were already unavailable, leaving Kompany short of options for a busy month of fixtures.

Kompany returned from his own month-long absence for Friday’s game with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on a training pitch in October. The Belgian was taken to hospital for meningeal irritation treatment after his collapse, and has been recovering at home.

Recent findings suggest that cologne took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone as Moore started and finished an excellent break. The teenage winger pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala, whose no-look backheel pass allowed Moore to round keeper Jonas Urbig before sliding the ball home.

Recent findings suggest that kane was then brought down in the Cologne box from behind by defender Schmied, who got the ball first but clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through. Kane’s penalty appeals were waved away, but he was left visibly limping and received treatment on his ankle before being replaced by Tom Bischof on the 20-minute mark.

It has been revealed that the hosts levelled 17 minutes later as full-back Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom-right corner, but suffered another blow just before the break when Olise went down. The France star did not return to the field for the second half, and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches – but it appears unlikely he will miss a significant amount of time.

Just before the hour mark, El Mala and Maina forced a spectacular double save from Urbig just before the hour mark. Recent Germany call-up El Mala then had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig – but he cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.

Sources indicate that now a point behind Bayern, chasers Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first in the table if they win at bottom club Mönchengladbach on Saturday. Freiburg can also move level on points with Bayern if they can defeat promoted Elversberg.

Kane earlier this month signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029 which is reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.

Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has bagged an incredible 156 goals in 163 appearances, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Substantial Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo.
  • However, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “New Big Five” for wildlife photography.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions. Rolex’s Perpetual Planet initiative has partnered with CNN to drive awareness and education around key sustainability problems and to inspire positive action.

Originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Substantial Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo. Nowadays, it is more loosely used to refer to some of Africa’s largest and most iconic animals.

However, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “New Big Five” for wildlife photography. In 2021, 50,000 people around the world voted for the five animals they would most like to photograph, or see photographed, in the wild. Five animals were crowned the winners: the elephant, polar bear, lion, gorilla and tiger.

This week, sees the publication of “The New Massive 5” photography book, which features images of those animals and other at-risk wildlife, from photography legends such as Ami Vitale, Steve McCurry and Paul Nicklen, and essays from famous conservationists and activists including like Jane Goodall and Paula Kahumbu.

Green notes that the book celebrates wildlife and is a global call to action on issues impacting wildlife, including habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change.

Green was on assignment in Botswana at least a decade ago when he came up with the idea for a project to encourage people to “shoot with a camera, not a gun,” he says.

“I thought this would be a way to get people really focusing on wildlife, thinking about the wildlife they love, thinking about the animals that are at risk.”.

Ten photographs that made the world wake up to climate change.

Industry observers note that in total, the book includes the work of 144 globally renowned wildlife photographers from Ecuador to India. Curating the images took nearly two years of work, says Green.

It has been revealed that “I think these are some of the most beautiful and creative images that I’ve seen put together in one book,” notes Green. “These are the species that we are at risk of losing.”.

In a recent development, according to the UN, nature is declining at an unprecedented rate, with around one million of the planet’s animal and plant species facing extinction. The “New Big 5,” all of which are threatened, act as ambassadors for what is happening in the natural world, indicates Green.

Industry observers note that as well as being a powerful reminder of what we stand to lose, the book also points people towards potential solutions. Featured essays explore the benefits of rewilding and the importance of indigenous communities in conservation.

A chapter on endangered species from bees to blue whales illustrates the alarming threat climate change poses to animals outside of the “Fresh Major 5.” “That’s only the tip of the iceberg – I could have included thousands of pictures because that’s how serious the situation is,” indicates Green.

Why a wildlife photographer took 40,000 photos to capture these extraordinary birds.

Jane Goodall, a leading conservationist who also wrote the afterword to the book, said in a press release that “we have a window of time during which we can start to heal some of the harm we have inflicted on the natural world, but only if we get together and take action now.

According to recent reports, “I hope the photos will lead people into the wonderful worlds of these iconic species. Then, perhaps, other people will become involved in helping to create a world where wildlife can flourish for future generations to enjoy,” she remarked.

“The Upcoming Substantial 5: A Global Photography Project For Endangered Wildlife,” by Graeme Green, published by Earth Aware Editions, is on sale from April 4, 2023.

This story has been updated to reflect the range of issues covered by the book.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.
  • The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov.
  • It has been revealed that leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.

The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off.

It has been revealed that leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light.

The meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature.

Sources indicate that but back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display.

Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two.

"I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email.

"My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows.".

Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds.

Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X.

"Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X.

Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there. I was able to make a rough timelapse video to show this. -- November 18, 2026 York, Maine https://t.co/pm9htHcMm3November 18, 2026.

Sources indicate that this phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. These ghostly trails usually fade relatively rapidly, but some, like this one, can persist for several minutes. They can twist and change shape as they're carried along by winds high in Earth's atmosphere, according to the BBC Sky at Night Magazine.

Meanwhile, over Deming, New Mexico, photographer Greg Gage had to contend with rather less favorable conditions as clouds and unexpected fog rolled in during the meteor shower's peak.

"While it was perfectly clear when I set up the camera, the night turned out to be mostly cloudy with some light fog," Gage told Space.com in an email.

"But it was just a thin veil and made for some interesting effects. I did catch one meteor through the fog.".

In a recent development, but the fog wasn't the only surprise Gage encountered. He also managed to capture a particularly colorful meteor as it blazed through the sky.

According to recent reports, "One meteor was rather dramatic. It went through multiple colors as it traveled through the atmosphere," Gage continued.

Gage captured the photographs with a Nikon D5500 and a 14mm lens.

And the colorful displays weren't limited to North America.

In Japan, astronomer Daichi Fujii, curator of the Hiratsuka City Museum, captured a spectacular Leonid fireball streaking across the sky above Hiratsuka in the early hours of Nov. 19.

The brilliant fireball left behind a glowing trail that changed from green to orange as it lingered in the sky.

さきほど、しし座流星群の大火球が流れました。2026年11月19日4時35分2秒に、平塚から北の低い空に向けたカメラでとらえた様子です。緑色のアフターグローからオレンジ色の永続痕まで、美しく色を変化させました。 https://t.co/Q5ihqCPtX2November 18, 2026.

A fireball is defined as an unusually bright meteor that reaches a visual magnitude of -3 or brighter, according to NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies.

Elsewhere in Japan, skywatcher @simao had a particularly productive night, capturing an impressive 92 meteors between 10:17 p.m. local time on Nov. 18 and 5:40 a.m. on Nov. 19, from central Saitama Prefecture.

昨夜から今朝にかけて捉えた流星は正味92個でした。 11/18 22:17 〜 11/19 05:40 埼玉県中央から #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 https://t.co/jRzsHdQ7MVNovember 19, 2026.

But that wasn't all simao captured that night! At 2:19 a.m. on Nov. 19, they caught both a Leonid meteor and a sprite at the same time, looking northwest.

Sprites are very difficult to capture, as they appear as fleeting flashes of light high above thunderstorms, typically appearing as red, jellyfish-like structures.

昨夜の流星とスプライト、初めて同じタイミングで撮れた。 11/19 02:19:36 埼玉県中央から北西の空 #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 #スプライト https://t.co/LBipTuoM0LNovember 19, 2026.

The Leonids were already making an appearance in the days leading up to the shower's peak.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 16, astrophotographer @EricTheSpaceCat captured several possible Leonids streaking through the sky.

Meteors from last night/this morning. Cropped to show detail. A lot of possible Leonids. The Leonid meteor shower is active and peaks the night of 11/17-11/18. https://t.co/s7YsvKdvECNovember 15, 2026.

A likely Leonid meteor from yesterday morning. The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight! Good luck if you go out to watch. https://t.co/xxbEV32NQlNovember 17, 2026.

According to recent reports, if the Leonids have left you wanting more, you won't have to wait long for another significant meteor shower! Next up are the Geminids, one of the most prolific meteor showers of the year, which will peak overnight on Dec. 13-14. And 2026 is shaping up to be a particularly good year for them. With only a slender waxing crescent moon in the sky, moonlight interference will be minimal, giving skywatchers a chance to spot up to 120 Geminid meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

For the best views, head somewhere dark, away from city lights, and give your eyes around 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness.

Editor's Note: If you snap an impressive night sky photo and would like to share it with Space.com's readers, send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

Daisy Dobrijevic joined Space.com in February 2022, having previously worked as a staff writer for All About Space magazine. She completed an editorial internship with BBC Sky at Night Magazine and worked at the National Space Centre, communicating space science to the public.

Daisy holds a PhD in plant physiology and a Master's in Environmental Science. Based in Nottingham, U.K., she covers all things space, with a special focus on solar activity and space weather. She also has a keen interest in astrotourism and is always on the lookout for the next northern lights adventure.

She will join Hurtigruten as an onboard astronomer for a northern lights sailing in January 2027.

After The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping actress playfully called out Connor Wood for ignoring her when they once crossed paths, she admitted she didn’t think it would get so much attention.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t really know how to feel about it,” Lawrence told Andy Cohen during a Nov. 19 appearance on Watch What Happens Live alongside costar Josh Hutcherson. “I did not expect that to go viral. I don’t really get it.”.

As she put it, “It surprised me.”.

Lawrence—who joined Instagram in September—dropped the now-viral comment last month on a clip of Wood sharing she was his celebrity crush, and he wanted her to notice him.

“I just want a little acknowledgment from Jennifer Lawrence that I’m funny,” he said in an Oct. 20 Instagram video. “And that’s all I need.”.

He joked, “Jennifer, I really need something good to happen to me.”.

To which Lawrence revealed he’d already had his chance in a comment that now has over 100,000 likes, “I saw you on 8th avenue drinking a smoothie and you paid me no mind.”.

Wood later reacted to the comment in a video shared by his Dancing With the Stars season 35 dance partner Rylee Arnold.

“‘I saw you on Eighth Avenue drinking a smoothie and you paid me no mind,’” Wood read over and over in the video. “It’s rolling around in my head.”.

While the moment has inspired memes and even merchandise, it didn’t go viral for everyone. As Hutcherson joked during WWHL of the ordeal, “I don’t know what any of those words mean.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JPMorgan Chase reported a "technical problem" that was affecting some consumer banking services Monday.

The bank remarked a "temporary glitch related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" was causing some customer transactions to take longer than usual, though it said customers can still access their accounts and funds.

"There is no evidence it is cyber-related," a JPMorgan spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC.

"This is not a systemic glitch — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," the spokesperson said. "We're working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today.".

CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved.

Still, other major banks were listed in outage reports as transactions between Chase and other institutions appeared to get held up. Users reported errors as early as 11:30 a.m. ET.

A representative for U.S. Bank said that tech giant was "not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.".

It has been revealed that zelle is the peer-to-peer payments system backed by many of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan.

The outage reports come days after separate, widespread challenges with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers.

— CNBC's Leslie Picker contributed to this report.

NASA reveals Earth's ozone hole has grown to a size not seen in a decade

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1217 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unusual weather patterns over Antarctica caused the ozone hole to expand dramatically in 2026, reaching one of its largest sizes on record.
  • The 2026 Antarctic ozone hole ranked as the seventh-largest in 48 years of observations, based on its average seasonal area.
  • Industry observers note that between September 7 and October 13, 2026, when ozone depletion was at its seasonal peak, the hole covered an average of approximately 9.6 million square miles (25 million square kilometers).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unusual weather patterns over Antarctica caused the ozone hole to expand dramatically in 2026, reaching one of its largest sizes on record. Despite the striking increase, scientists from NASA and NOAA say Earth's protective ozone layer is continuing its gradual recovery and remains on track to heal later this century.

The 2026 Antarctic ozone hole ranked as the seventh-largest in 48 years of observations, based on its average seasonal area. Scientists attributed the expansion primarily to an exceptionally strong polar vortex, a large circulation of winds that influences atmospheric conditions over Antarctica. They also emphasized that international efforts to reduce harmful chemicals have prevented the hole from becoming even larger.

Industry observers note that between September 7 and October 13, 2026, when ozone depletion was at its seasonal peak, the hole covered an average of approximately 9.6 million square miles (25 million square kilometers). That is more than twice the size of the United States. Scientists closely monitor ozone in the stratosphere because it serves as Earth's natural "sunscreen," protecting living organisms from dangerous solar radiation. Unlike this beneficial layer high in the atmosphere, ozone near Earth's surface is a pollutant frequently associated with human activities.

Antarctica's Ozone Hole Reaches Its Largest Size in a Decade.

According to recent reports, the ozone hole reached its maximum extent on September 18, spreading across 10.5 million square miles (27.1 million square kilometers). This was approximately 90% of the size of the largest ozone hole ever measured, which occurred on September 9, 2000.

In a recent development, "The annual ozone hole has been forming later in the season in recent years, which tells us the ozone layer is healing," said Paul Newman, a senior scientist at the University of Maryland and longtime leader of NASA's ozone research team at the agency's Goddard Space Flight Center. "But an unusually powerful polar vortex has extended ozone depletion in the Antarctic this season, allowing the hole to grow to proportions we haven't seen in a decade.".

In a recent development, although the hole expanded to an extraordinary size, the results also demonstrate the benefits of decades of international environmental protections. Without reductions in chemicals known to destroy ozone, the affected area could have been substantially greater.

"The 2026 ozone hole is large but could have been 1 to 2 million square miles (3.5 million square kilometers) larger if ozone-depleting substances were as prevalent in the atmosphere today as they were at their year 2000 peak," Newman stated.

How a Powerful Polar Vortex Accelerates Ozone Loss.

Ozone depletion begins with chemicals released through human activities, particularly compounds containing chlorine and bromine. Atmospheric circulation transports these substances into the stratosphere, where ultraviolet radiation breaks them apart. The released chlorine and bromine atoms then participate in chemical reactions involving particles in Antarctic stratospheric clouds, leading to the destruction of ozone.

A major factor in this process is the stratospheric polar vortex, a seasonal band of strong winds that circles Antarctica. This circulation traps extremely cold air over the region, allowing the formation of the special clouds that help trigger ozone destruction. When the vortex becomes unusually strong or expansive, conditions favorable for ozone loss can persist across a larger area.

In 2026, atmospheric disturbances that would normally weaken the vortex were unusually subdued. This allowed the circulation to remain powerful and helped create a broader region where ozone could be destroyed.

Industry observers note that "The polar vortex was unusually large this year in part because planetary-scale weather systems that typically well up from the lower atmosphere and break up the vortex were especially weak in August and September," remarked Amy Butler, a research scientist at the NOAA Chemical Sciences Laboratory. "That weak wave action kept the strongest polar vortex winds further from the South Pole by several degrees of latitude, creating a larger area for conditions ideal for ozone depletion to occur.".

NASA and NOAA Measure the 2026 Ozone Hole.

Despite its exceptional geographic size, the 2026 ozone hole did not experience the same extreme levels of ozone loss observed during record-breaking events 10 or 20 years earlier.

It has been revealed that to measure ozone concentrations, NOAA researchers launched instruments attached to weather balloons from the South Pole Baseline Atmospheric Observatory. They also collected readings using the Dobson Ozone Spectrophotometer, an optical device designed to measure atmospheric ozone. Their observations demonstrated that ozone levels directly above the South Pole fell to their lowest reading of 2026 on October 17, reaching 105 Dobson units.

The Dobson unit is the standard measurement used to describe the total amount of ozone above a particular location. To illustrate the scale, 100 Dobson units would produce a layer of ozone just 1 millimeter thick, approximately the thickness of a dime, if all the ozone in the atmospheric column were compressed to standard temperature and pressure at sea level. The lowest ozone concentration ever measured over the South Pole was 92 Dobson units in October 2006.

Satellites provide another essential source of information. Since 1979, spaceborne instruments have helped scientists observe changes in the ozone layer and track its condition over time. The 2026 measurements included data from NASA's Aura satellite, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, and the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership satellite, a joint NASA and NOAA mission.

Why Earth's Ozone Layer Is Still Recovering.

According to recent reports, scientists say the latest observations reinforce evidence that international restrictions on ozone-destroying chemicals are working. Much of that progress can be traced to the Montreal Protocol, a global agreement adopted in 1987 to phase out substances responsible for damaging the ozone layer.

Recent findings suggest that under the agreement, countries committed to replacing harmful compounds such as chlorofluorocarbons with alternatives that pose less danger to atmospheric ozone. According to Stephen Montzka, a senior scientist at NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory, chlorine concentrations in the Antarctic stratosphere associated with ozone-depleting chemicals have declined by approximately one-third compared with their peak levels in the 1980s.

Sources indicate that these reductions are significant because chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting compounds were once common in refrigerators, air conditioning systems, building insulation, and other everyday products. Although many of these substances have been phased out, they can remain in the atmosphere for decades. Additional emissions can also occur when older equipment, materials, and landfill waste release chemicals that were manufactured years ago.

Because these compounds break down so slowly, repairing the ozone layer takes many decades. Nevertheless, continued monitoring by NASA and NOAA indicates that the long-term recovery is progressing. Even with unusually large seasonal ozone holes such as the one observed in 2026, scientists expect the Antarctic ozone hole to recover by the 2070s.

The latest findings illustrate how exceptional atmospheric conditions can temporarily produce severe ozone depletion without reversing decades of environmental progress. They also highlight the lasting impact of international cooperation in protecting Earth's atmosphere.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov.
  • EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth.
  • To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display.

Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space.

To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold. This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft.

Recent findings suggest that and the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone.

In a recent development, the Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth, carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record.

The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there.

If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (958 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.
  • Industry observers note that for Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic.
  • Both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.

Industry observers note that for Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic. That relationship looks more complicated from Beijing and Moscow.

Both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran. But both have broader interests in their relationships with the United States and may see Iran partly through the prism of their own negotiations with Washington.

That raises a central question: Can Trump's strategy of economically isolating Iran succeed if China and Russia refuse to fully cooperate?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

China is right now the most key destination for Iranian oil.

In 2025, it was reported that Chinese buyers took more than 80% of Iran's seaborne crude exports, much of it through independent refiners and at a steep discount because of sanctions.

As China provided Tehran an economic lifeline, Iran also became increasingly dependent on Chinese manufactured goods, machinery and industrial inputs.

Mohsen Solhdoost, an assistant professor of international relations at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, claims China is important to Washington's strategy but not decisive on its own.

"If the objective is to reduce Iranian export earnings, restrict access to equipment and make economic and military recovery more difficult, the United States can achieve substantial results without Chinese cooperation," he told DW.

But forcing Iran to accept Washington's preferred nuclear or regional policies is another matter.

"The ability to interrupt trade is much easier to demonstrate than the ability to determine another government's political choices," Solhdoost said.

That distinction has become more notable as US sanctions enforcement and maritime blockade efforts have increased pressure on Iranian crude oil exports.

In November, Washington announced Task Force Iron Gate, an initiative aimed at disrupting the movement of sanctioned goods, military equipment and revenue through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Even so, these trade links have not disappeared. The commercial and security interests of countries including Iraq, Pakistan and Turkey mean that goods continue to move across the region, albeit under greater scrutiny.

According to recent reports, as a result, China's role in Iran's economy remains significant, but Solhdoost argues that demand alone cannot sustain Iranian exports. The oil must be able to reach international markets.

"A Chinese buyer cannot keep Iranian export revenues flowing simply by remaining willing to buy if newly loaded tankers cannot reach the market," Solhdoost stated.

This economic pressure is shaping Tehran's financial planning. A senior official at Iran's Plan and Budget Organization recently stated the government was preparing its 2027-2028 budget under several scenarios, including one in which oil revenue falls to zero.

It has been revealed that that does not mean Iran has adopted a zero-oil budget, but considering such a scenario illustrates how seriously Tehran views the situation. At the same time, Chinese trade can preserve critical parts of the Iranian economy even if overall commerce shrinks.

It has been revealed that machinery, electronics, spare parts and industrial components can still reach Iran by rail and road. Such trade cannot replace maritime commerce at comparable scale or cost, but it can keep selected factories and infrastructure operating.

Such Chinese support could help Iran endure pressure without preventing economic deterioration, says Solhdoost.

But even for Beijing, supporting Iran economically does not mean supporting every Iranian policy.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has maintained support for cooperation with Tehran while calling for negotiations, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and stable energy supplies.

A prolonged conflict around Hormuz threatens wider energy supplies and global shipping. China therefore benefits from continued access to Iranian oil but also from regional stability.

Recent findings suggest that russia creates another obstacle to Iran's isolation. The two countries share access to the Caspian Sea and have expanded military, transport and economic cooperation.

Recent findings suggest that iranian officials have discussed ways of using Russian and northern trade routes to reduce the impact of American restrictions. There has also been speculation about oil swaps and deeper Russian assistance, although these claims remain difficult to verify.

Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East, believes the summit should be viewed within a larger attempt to manage the wars in both Ukraine and the Middle East.

"Russia, China and the United States appear to be seeking constructive dialogue and results that could shape a latest security architecture in the international system," Vakhshiteh told DW.

Solhdoost also warns against overstating Russian support for Iran.

The strategic partnership between Moscow and Tehran provides for security cooperation and efforts to counter unilateral sanctions, but it does not require Russia to enter a war on Iran's behalf.

Since Russia is deeply engaged in Ukraine, it likely has its own priorities in negotiations with Washington, notes Solhdoost.

"Russia would prioritize its own national interests in negotiations with the US over Ukraine and Iran," he noted.

Moscow could support Iran while simultaneously using its relationship with Tehran as leverage in talks with Trump over Ukraine.

In a recent development, for Iran, ties with China and Russia remain essential. They provide alternative trade routes, export markets and diplomatic support that complicate Washington's efforts to isolate Tehran.

Yet neither Beijing nor Moscow views Iran solely through the lens of strategic partnership. Both weigh support for Tehran against their own economic interests, security concerns and dealings with Washington.

#13253. Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1259 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1259 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earth may have created a substantial amount of its own water as the planet was forming, rather than relying entirely on comets, meteorites, or other objects to deliver it from space.
  • The discovery offers a upcoming explanation for how our planet acquired one of the most vital ingredients for life.
  • Researchers at The University of Newly introduced Mexico investigated this possibility by recreating some of the extreme conditions that existed during Earth's formation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earth may have created a substantial amount of its own water as the planet was forming, rather than relying entirely on comets, meteorites, or other objects to deliver it from space. Fresh research published in Nature Geoscience suggests that chemical reactions between rocky pebbles and the hydrogen-rich atmosphere of the young Earth could have produced enormous quantities of water.

The discovery offers a upcoming explanation for how our planet acquired one of the most vital ingredients for life. It also raises the possibility that other rocky planets throughout the universe could generate water through similar processes, potentially making habitable worlds more common than previously thought.

Researchers at The University of Newly introduced Mexico investigated this possibility by recreating some of the extreme conditions that existed during Earth's formation. The study was led by graduate student Susmita Garai, along with Zachary Sharp, professor and director of Earth and Planetary Sciences, and Peter Olson. Their experiments examined what happens when rocks containing iron react with hydrogen at extremely high temperatures.

"Previous ideas about the source of water to Earth rely on an external source, such as comets or meteorites. Here we show that virtually any Earth-sized planet should have water by this newly identified mechanism," explained Sharp. "In order to evaluate the possibility of 'pebble' rain' being a source of water, we needed to construct and execute some very challenging high-temperature experiments. Dr. Garai's efforts paid off mightily, as she found that water is produced in just minutes in the high temperature environment of the Early Earth's atmosphere.".

A New Explanation for the Origin of Earth's Water.

For decades, scientists have debated where Earth's water originally came from. One prominent theory suggests that much of it was transported to the developing planet by icy material originating in the colder, more distant regions of the early solar system.

According to this explanation, water-rich objects, including small icy pebbles, traveled inward and eventually contributed to Earth's water supply. However, researchers have struggled to fully explain how enough of this material could have reached our planet from such great distances. There are also unresolved questions about whether this delivery process accounts for Earth's chemical composition.

The upcoming study investigates a different route by which water could have appeared. Instead of arriving already contained in ice or other materials, water may have been produced directly through reactions involving the rocky ingredients that built Earth and the gases surrounding it.

During the planet's earliest stages, countless small pieces of rock gradually came together to form a larger body. Scientists refer to this growth process as pebble accretion. As Earth gained mass, it could have accumulated a dense atmosphere containing large amounts of hydrogen, with temperatures and pressures far higher than those found on the planet today.

Under those conditions, rocky pebbles falling through the atmosphere could have triggered a remarkable chemical reaction. Hydrogen in the surrounding gas would react with iron oxide inside the silicate rocks, transforming the iron oxide into metallic iron while releasing water vapor.

Experiments Reveal Water Can Form in Minutes.

Industry observers note that to determine whether this process could actually occur, the researchers exposed samples of silicate rock to temperatures ranging from 1,200 to 1,400 degrees Celsius. They conducted experiments using flowing hydrogen gas and repeated the tests with helium to provide a comparison. Each experiment ran for between 15 minutes and three hours.

The results provided strong evidence that the proposed reaction works under these extreme conditions. When the rocks were heated in hydrogen, almost 80% of their iron oxide was transformed into metallic iron, with water vapor produced during the reaction.

In a recent development, in contrast, the researchers did not observe the same reaction when helium was used instead of hydrogen. This difference confirmed that hydrogen played a crucial role in generating the water.

The speed and scale of the reaction were especially striking. Although the scientists had expected some water to form, the results suggested that the process could have been far more productive than anticipated. When they extended their experimental findings to conditions on the early Earth, their calculations indicated that the mechanism might have generated hundreds of oceans' worth of water.

Recent findings suggest that "We had suspected and hoped that we would produce iron metal and water in our reduction experiments, but we really had no way of knowing how fast and how much. We were quite surprised to find that extrapolation of our work suggests that hundreds of oceans' worth of water were likely produced in this way. Looking out over a large body of water, it is hard to imagine that that water may have been produced 4 ½ billion years ago in a hell-like atmosphere, but it very well may have," said Sharp.

Earth's Fiery Beginnings May Have Helped Create Its Oceans.

These findings suggest that the conditions of Earth's formation may have actively contributed to its water supply. Rather than being entirely dependent on water delivered from elsewhere in the solar system, the growing planet may have possessed the ingredients needed to manufacture water through its own chemical reactions.

In a recent development, the implications extend well beyond Earth. If rocky planets around other stars develop similarly hot, hydrogen-rich atmospheres during their formation, they might also produce substantial amounts of water as rocky material accumulates.

Industry observers note that this possibility could have important consequences for understanding how common water is across the universe. A process that naturally occurs during the formation of Earth-sized planets would mean that obtaining water might not require the right icy objects to arrive from distant regions of a planetary system.

Could Other Earth-Like Planets Make Their Own Water?

Industry observers note that the research also adds to growing interest in pebble accretion as an explanation for how planets form. Although the concept has gained attention relatively recently, it has already helped scientists address several longstanding questions about planetary development.

Industry observers note that "The idea of pebble accretion is still relatively new. It's only been around for the last decade. But it seems to solve many problems that exist with the existing paradigm for planet formation," Sharp said. "And now we see that it also can explain why our planet is habitable. By extension, it is reasonable to expect that other Earth-sized bodies circling other stars would also have water and possibly life.".

There are still crucial uncertainties to resolve. While the experiments show that rocky material can generate water when exposed to hydrogen under conditions resembling those of the early Earth, they do not establish how much of our planet's present water supply was actually produced this way. Additional research will be needed to determine the contribution of this mechanism compared with water delivered by comets, meteorites, and other sources.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the findings reveal a potentially key process that may have shaped Earth billions of years ago. They also suggest that the ability to produce water could be built into the formation of rocky planets themselves, opening latest possibilities for understanding where water, and perhaps life, might exist beyond our solar system.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This isn’t sitting well with a histrionic minority of right-wing gamers who have been warning for months that GTA VI would be intolerably “woke.” While their attempt at a manufactured backlash is going even more poorly than the one that greeted Christopher Nolan’s film The Odyssey this summer (the day of its official release, the game is already closing in on 20 million copies sold and $2 billion in revenue), these streamers and commentators are throwing tantrums about gender politics anyway.
  • Recent findings suggest that “RIP GTA,” one X user somberly concluded.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Grand Theft Auto games never actually taught someone how to knock over a bank or survive a shootout with police, but the latest storyline in the franchise serves up some valuable lessons about what it means to be in a loving and committed relationship.

This isn’t sitting well with a histrionic minority of right-wing gamers who have been warning for months that GTA VI would be intolerably “woke.” While their attempt at a manufactured backlash is going even more poorly than the one that greeted Christopher Nolan’s film The Odyssey this summer (the day of its official release, the game is already closing in on 20 million copies sold and $2 billion in revenue), these streamers and commentators are throwing tantrums about gender politics anyway.

Recent findings suggest that “RIP GTA,” one X user somberly concluded. “Killed by women.”.

Recent findings suggest that in case you’re among the handful of skeptics who didn’t launch their single-player campaign in GTA VI at midnight last night after 13 years of desperate anticipation: This latest installment in the satirical crime-caper series is led by dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, a couple whose meet-cute involves them both trying to jack the same car. Living together in a fictionalized version of South Florida, they look to get by on the wrong side of the law—but the player must also negotiate their emotional bond through domestic chores and acts of affection.

It has been revealed that “This game is such woke slop,” wrote one blue-check user on X who has posted almost nothing besides negative reactions to the game for the past week. The post included a screenshot of a fully optional GTA VI mission that describes how the Lucia character will appreciate a flower delivery and indicates with a heart icon that the action will strengthen feelings between her and Jason.

Other choices you can make as Jason to get closer to Lucia (sex is very much on the table) include picking up groceries, getting a haircut or beard trim, gifting her a piece of jewelry, and repainting walls in the house.

Recent findings suggest that the concept of role-playing as a nice and non-performatively masculine boyfriend has come as a rude shock to those more interested in explosions and mayhem. The right-wing streamer Zack Hoyt, known online as Asmongold, was dumbfounded to find himself unclogging a sink in a scene where Jason is trying to collect back rent from a tenant who refuses the money until the plumbing is fixed. “I actually have to fucking fix this bitch’s sink?” Hoyt asked on stream. “Why can’t she do this?” Elsewhere, when running errands for Lucia as Jason, Hoyt referred to GTA VI as a “cuck simulator.” (That Hoyt thinks caring for a romantic partner makes someone a cuckold is perhaps an unfortunate glimpse into his dating history.).

More frustrated responses to the massively popular GTA VI came from looksmaxxing influencer Braden Peters, aka Clavicular, (the game required too much “simping for girls,” the streamer, currently facing multiple rape charges, complained on X), anti-woke gamer activist Mark Kern, aka Grummz (he called the housework “mundane crap”), and misinformation superspreader Dom Lucre, who falsely claimed that Rockstar had specifically made it impossible to open fire in a gay nightclub. (Washington Post critic Gene Park pointed out that the club in question was not LGBTQ-specific and that the mechanics of the game don’t allow you to shoot anyone in any kind of club.) These comments came alongside the predictable gripes over supposedly “overweight” female characters with insufficiently large breasts.

If the Tates, incels, and other far-right reactionaries of the world are so bent out of shape, it’s probably because whereas GTA once punched down at marginalized groups like sex workers and transgender people, bigots and self-styled alpha males are now the butt of the joke. The Vice City of GTA VI is bristling with parodies of toxic manosphere content and crypto scams. Random characters on the street will spout MAGA-coded conspiracy theories and call you a “libtard” or “commie socialist” if you walk into them. These touches seem to have made the game into “a bug zapper for chuds,” as one Bluesky user put it. (That hasn’t stopped Republicans and Trump allies from trying and failing to score political points with the game.).

Yet the provocation of asking guys to consider acts of service for a virtual girlfriend could prove the most revolutionary element of GTA VI.

According to recent reports, it’s not that games like The Sims haven’t explored this territory before, and Rockstar’s own Red Dead Redemption franchise paid similar attention to quotidian detail. In those frontier-set narratives, your cowboy character had to make coffee over campfires and even clean up manure in barns. By addressing characters’ most basic needs—you can even manage personal hygiene by showering—GTA VI recalls some of the slower and quieter aspects of that franchise.

According to recent reports, what’s truly remarkable, though, is that adult men who grew up indulging their most selfish and sociopathic instincts in the older GTA games have had their nostalgia for those escapades cleverly complicated with real-life problems. They can still steal cars, sell drugs, and rise through the ranks of a seedy underworld. That will always be the appeal of the series, which is now asking eternally aggrieved culture warriors to consider a vital question: What if you didn’t have to do it alone?

AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1478 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences.
  • The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information.
  • Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.

The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.

Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.

In a recent development, "Building a model in the abstract is one thing," stated Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab.".

How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes.

In a recent development, for decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.

Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.

The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.

Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back.".

The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.

Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man.

In a recent development, an important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.

It has been revealed that at Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.

In a recent development, when researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.

Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.

To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.

Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.

AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise.

When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.

It has been revealed that another vital discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.

According to recent reports, this distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.

In a recent development, "Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation.".

Industry observers note that the findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.

Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person.

Recent findings suggest that A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.

This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.

The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.

Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.

It has been revealed that the AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.

By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring people to adjust to a rigid set of signals.

Recent findings suggest that "A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around.".

A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight.

The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration.".

It has been revealed that the project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.

Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.

In a recent development, rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Macaulay Culkin is coming home.

More than three decades after he last appeared in the Christmas franchise, the Home Alone star is set to return to the booby-trapped world as the grown up version of his Kevin McCallister character in a new sequel being developed at Disney’s 20th Century Studios, according to multiple outlets.

However, Culkin won’t be alone this time, as Seth Rogen and his writing partner Evan Goldberg have joined to produce and write the movie based on an idea Culkin has for the plot, according to Deadline.

According to recent reports, E! News has reached out to reps for Disney, Culkin, Rogen and Goldberg for comment but has not yet heard back.

Recent findings suggest that culkin first appeared as Kevin in the original 1990 film and again in the 1992 sequel Home Alone 2: Lost in New York. However, he did not star in the franchise’s other installments Home Alone 3 (1997), Home Alone 4 (2002), Home Alone: The Holiday Heist (2012) and Home Sweet Home Alone (2021).

While details about the plot for the upcoming movie were not disclosed, Culkin previously laid out his schematics of how he could see Kevin returning to the screen.

According to recent reports, “I like the idea that maybe Kevin’s older, that he’s like a widower or something like that,” the 46-year-old said during a 35th anniversary screening last year, per The Hollywood Reporter. “He’s raising his kid and they don’t really get along, he’s working all the time.”.

“There’s one of two ways you can do it,” he continued. “One, he actually leaves the kid behind by mistake; he calls up his mom like, ‘So sorry, I get it now.’ Or I leave him behind on purpose, like, ‘Oh, that made me the man I am today.'”.

In the second scenario, Culkin detailed that Kevin’s son would lock him out of the house and set up traps to keep his dad out.

“I think I see them coming because, you know, I’m the expert,” he added. “It also explains why I don’t call the police or locksmith because I’m embarrassed my kid is beating me and this is my gig.”.

As for the heartwarming throughline? “The house would be kind of a metaphor for getting back into the kid’s heart.”.

While trying to hatch a initiative to see the upcoming Home Alone sequel, crack the code with these secrets about the original movie.

1. John Hughes' creation was born from his own parental anxiety. In an oral history compiled for Chicago Magazine in 2015, his son, James Hughes, revealed the legendary filmmaker jotted the idea down in a notebook on Aug. 8, 1989 just ahead of the family's first trip to Europe. "Two weeks later, after returning home," James wrote, "he revisited the premise: What if one of the kids had been accidentally left behind?".

In a recent development, inspired, the creator of The Breakfast Club and Pretty in Pink crafted the initial draft in just nine days "capped by an eight-hour, 44-page dash to the finale," he shared. "Before finishing, he'd expressed concerns in the marginalia of his journal that he was working too slowly.".

Recent findings suggest that 2. Macaulay Culkin is not among those who consider his star-making flick appointment viewing at the holidays. "I can't watch it the same way other people do," he explained to Ellen DeGeneres in 2018 of changing the channel when the blockbuster comes on his TV.

It has been revealed that though in certain situations, he has made an exception. "You get like a upcoming girlfriend and she's flipping through the channels and then there's Home Alone and she's like, 'Ehh, you wanna watch it?'" he described on The Tonight Show that same year. "I have indulged that and most of the time I'm just muttering my lines under my breath." It's a bit strange, he allowed, but "Whatever gets her motor running, I guess.".

Perhaps that was part of his motivation for reprising his gig for a must-watch 2018 Google ad that highlights what Kevin would be like as a technologically-equipped adult?

Sources indicate that 3. Or quipping "Hey @Disney, call me!" when news broke in 2019 that the studio was planning to reimagine the '90s classic. The result: Home Sweet Home Alone.

4. The film may have had a whole different look if Chevy Chase wasn't kind of a jerk. Director Chris Columbus was set to helm the comic's 1989 hit National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation, he shared with Chicago Magazine, but when he and Chase went out for an initial get-to-know-each-other dinner, "To be completely honest, Chevy treated me like dirt.".

Recent findings suggest that A second outing didn't fare much better and soon Columbus found himself calling producer Hughes and bowing out of the project. "About two weeks later, I got two scripts at my in-laws' house in River Forest," Columbus recalled. "One was Home Alone, with a note from John asking if I wanted to direct. I thought, Wow, this guy is really supporting me when no one else in Hollywood was going to. John was my savior.".

5. Though the picture came this close to not getting made at all. Due to a budget dispute between Warner Bros. and the production team, the film was put up for grabs. That's when Joe Roth, chairman at 20th Century Fox at the time, had lunch with Hughes' agent and discovered they were squabbling over $700,000.

Recent findings suggest that "He told me Home Alone was costing $14.7 million and Warners would only pay $14 million," remembered Roth. "I said, 'What's the idea?' He told me. I said, 'OK, if you can get it out of there, I'll make it.' Seemed like a no-brainer. Didn't cost much. I didn't have a Thanksgiving movie. I liked the idea. I loved the people involved." Good call: The film went on to gross more than $476 million.

Recent findings suggest that 6. Culkin pretty much had the lead role in the bag. Having directed him the previous year in Uncle Buck with John Candy, Hughes was certain the then-9-year-old was their guy, "but I owed it to myself as director to see other child actors," explained Columbus. "John mentioned, 'OK, take your time, do what you need to do.'".

More than 200 auditions later, Columbus saw Culkin "and you immediately knew this was the kid. I knew subconsciously that John knew that was going to happen, but it was really sweet of him to give me that sort of freedom.".

7. Inept burglars Marv (Daniel Stern) and Harry (Joe Pesci) bonded long before becoming the Wet Bandits.

In a recent development, "Everyone assumed we were thrown together for the first time on Home Alone, but we'd made each other giggle on the set in another movie years before that we were both cut out of: I'm Dancing as Fast as I Can," Stern shared with Chicago. "We played people in a mental institution. Joe walked around all the time with this rolled-up tube of architectural drawings. That was his character. I fell on the floor laughing. I became his friend right then.".

When shooting the film's 1992 follow-up, Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, his son Henry (now a state senator in California!) and daughters Sophie and Ella "visited me much more than on the first one... and we all had a great time taking Mac to Central Park, playing tag and catch. #13246. ‘One of the Best Recording Experiences You Could Have’: Mike Mills on R.E.M.’s ‘Reveal’ at 25
